options.text: It stands in second position in the main clause.
It stands in second position after the subject.
options.misconception: confuses subject-first order with verb-second rule

options.text: It stands at the very end of the clause after the object.
options.misconception: treats "It stands at the very end of the clause after the…" as if it followed from the evidence

options.text: It stands immediately before the subject.
options.misconception: substitutes a familiar but inapplicable case for the relation the passage establishes

questions.explanation: German main clauses follow verb-second order, so the finite verb occupies the second structural position. The tempting idea that it always comes last applies only to subordinate clauses.

options.text: Yes, the verb is at the end.
Yes, because the subject is first.
No, the verb must be in second position.

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: main clauses require verb-second; verb-final belongs to subordinate clauses.
